front.title: Verification of Routes Using Region Authorization

abstract.t:
BGP routing security is a critical issue affecting the stability and reliability of Internet services. Existing mechanisms, including Route Origin Authorization (ROA) and Autonomous System Provider Authorization (ASPA), effectively mitigate route origin hijacking, path hijacking, and route leaks in general scenarios. However, in real-world deployments, large Internet Service Providers (ISPs) managing multiple Autonomous Systems (ASes) remain vulnerable. Attacking networks can exploit carefully crafted routes to bypass ROA and ASPA validations, causing traffic hijacking within or between large ISPs.
This document defines a region-based authorization and verification framework for multi-AS ISPs to prevent intra-ISP and inter-ISP traffic hijacking.
